key_insight: Optimized surface-code memory on a cloud-accessible IBM processor suppressed logical errors as the protected code distance increased from 3 to 6.
engineering_relevance: Readout, reset, and echo design can materially improve quantum memory performance, motivating joint optimization of QPU hardware and error-correction circuits.
method: Test rotated surface-code memories across placements on an IBM Nighthawk r2 processor.
Combine short readout, fused measurement and reset, and XX echo on data qubits during ancilla readout.
Evaluate distance scaling with maximum-likelihood decoding and memory experiments up to 150 rounds.
evidence_signal: Increasing the protected distance from 3 to 6 while holding the other distance fixed reduced per-round logical error from 0.53% to 0.24% in Z memory and from 0.52% to 0.22% in X memory.
watch_item: Performance varied by processor placement, and the distance advantage weakened in longer runs alongside long-lived correlations that may indicate persistent errors.
paper_title: Demonstration of Logical Error Suppression in a Surface Code Memory on a Cloud-Accessible IBM Superconducting Processor
